text:
alex: Quick idea — instead of stuffing more headers into the main safetensors/index, what if we ship a tiny per-shard "aux" sidecar? compact JSON/binary with: checksums, layer offsets (relative), quant profile tag, a lease id, and an optional signed manifest. would let runtime warmup do a cheap probe before heavy io.

sofia: @alex curious — main win is fewer mmap/parse passes on cold start? how does this interact with on-disk packing (bundles) and gzipped transports?

alex: yeah + cheaper verification. probe reads aux (small), decide whether to do index-first or stream fallback. auxiliaries can be appended to bundles as a separate file: shard-000.aux. gzipped bundles can include the aux uncompressed or compressed separately.

remi: two quick tradeoffs: 1) compatibility — older loaders must ignore aux (ok) but new loader must find aux in many locations (sidecar, inside bundle, S3 metadata). 2) atomicity — we need a clear write-order to avoid mismatch between weights and aux. suggestion: write aux last and use a short commit file (shard-000.aux.commit -> contains version+sig).

kevin: +1 on commit file. also think about eviction/lease: runtime nodes should acquire a lease id from aux so they can gossip "hotstart in progress" and avoid multiple nodes fetching same heavy shard. but that means aux updates on lease transitions — do we allow ephemeral lease writes to object storage? expensive.

sofia: maybe leases live in the runtime metadata store (etcd/consul) and aux only carries a stable boot-id + verification fingerprint. runtime uses internal lease service; aux only used for first-read decisions. keeps object storage writes cheap.

alex: good separation — aux = read-only artifact for verification/heuristics. runtime lease = ephemeral and not stored in object storage. but we still want signed aux so we can trust fingerprint without downloading whole shard.

remi: signatures + short fingerprint solves safety. one more: what about Mmap-friendly offsets? if aux includes absolute byte offsets for mmap, then bundling/repacking breaks them. prefer relative offsets from start-of-array-within-shard and an abi version.

kevin: implementation sketch:
```
shard-000.aux.json -> {
  "abi": "1",
  "layers": [{"name":"attn.wq","offset":1024,"length":8192}],
  "fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "quant_tag": "q8h",
  "signed_by": "redwood-release-v2"
}
shard-000.aux.commit -> {"ready": true, "ts": 1711119000}
```

alex: rollout plan: 1) accept aux when present (silent fallback when missing) 2) runtime uses aux for pref path heuristics 3) opt-in tooling to produce signed aux in model bundles 4) add docs + small CI check to ensure aux.commit exists before publish.

ops-bot: heads-up: anything that relies on signed metadata will need release automation updates (registry + signing key perms). filing infra ticket infra/1234.

sofia: sounds sane. one lingering question: do we version the aux schema per-model or per-shard? leaning per-shard (abi in aux) so loaders can fast-fail if incompatible.

alex: agreed. good enough to start with shard-level abi. i'll write a short RFC follow-up with the implementation sketch and list of file locations (sidecar, in-bundle, s3-metadata). thanks all. :thumbsup:
